title: Petra and the Hollow
premise: Paloma Eriksen, a mercenary bound to the silent god Vess and keeper of ledgers for a guild that trades in impossible things, discovers that the old gods are answering prayers again—and that Vess's silence was not death but imprisonment. As the usurper's armies march on the free cities, Paloma learns their guild's greatest asset is a door out of a country that officially no longer exists, and that opening it requires settling every debt in the ledgers, including the one owed for a massacre Paloma committed in Vess's name. Hunted by an inquisitor who was once their lover, Paloma must choose between restoring a god who demands atrocity and breaking their oath to save the people the ledger says they owe. In the end, Paloma burns the ledgers, unbinds Vess into forgetting, and holds the door open long enough for the free cities' refugees to pass through—staying behind as its last unpaid debt.
about_author: C. M. Kavanagh is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging the property records of dissolved nations before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town whose name has changed four times in two hundred years.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unanswered Names
chapters.summary: Paloma audits the guild's ledgers in the free city of Corvane, recording impossible trades: bottled grief, borrowed luck, a year of someone else's childhood. A prayer slips through their fingers mid-entry—the first answered prayer in twenty years. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath routine, the sense that stillness is ending.

chapters.title: Salt and Silver
chapters.summary: Paloma delivers a payment to the drowned chapel where they swore their oath to Vess, finding fresh offerings left by strangers—worship returning to a god everyone believes dead. The guildmaster, Ivetta, orders them to investigate who is praying. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: dread dressed as duty; the past knocking politely.

chapters.title: What the Usurper Wants
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Sera Halvard arrives in Corvane under a truce banner, seeking records of pre-conquest Vess-worship. She and Paloma share a charged, wary reunion—lovers before the conquest split them. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: love sharpened into suspicion; old tenderness weaponized by new loyalties.

chapters.title: A Debt in Ash
chapters.summary: Paloma finds the ledger page for the village of Merrow's Bend—the massacre they carried out in Vess's silent years, recorded as a debt never collected. The ink has begun moving on its own. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: guilt made physical; the horror that memory itself is waking up.

chapters.title: The Guild of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Ivetta convenes the guild's partners: a cartographer of vanished places, a thief who steals names, a priest of three dead gods. They reveal the Hollow—a door out of a country erased from maps—and that only settled debts can open it. POV: rotating council scene anchored in Paloma. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; hope with a price tag.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered Badly
chapters.summary: Across the free cities, answered prayers curdle: a fisherman's wish drowns his neighbors, a child's plea for her mother back returns something wearing her face. Paloma realizes Vess is answering through stolen memories. POV: interlaced vignettes converging on Paloma. Emotional beat: mounting dread; divinity as predation.

chapters.title: Sera's Confession
chapters.summary: Sera corners Paloma at night—not to arrest them but to confess she has been hearing Vess too, and that the usurper's armies march because he wants to cage the returning gods. She offers Paloma a way out if they surrender the ledgers. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: love against duty, both bleeding; betrayal offered gently.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Country
chapters.summary: The cartographer shows Paloma the map of the country that no longer exists—Vess's own nation, unwritten by treaty. The Hollow opens onto it, and the god's silence is explained: Vess was locked outside reality with everything erased. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: awe and vertigo; geography as wound.

chapters.title: Collecting the First Debt
chapters.summary: To settle Merrow's Bend, Paloma seeks the sole survivor, now an old woman selling charms in a border market. She does not want vengeance—she wants to remember her village, which the erasure took from her mind. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: mercy stranger than forgiveness; justice outside any law.

chapters.title: Armies on the Salt Road
chapters.summary: The usurper's vanguard reaches the free cities' outskirts. Ivetta orders the guild to begin closing accounts and preparing the Hollow, but the thief of names defects to Sera's side, taking the guild's most dangerous page. POV: Ivetta, then Paloma. Emotional beat: the machinery of war grinding closer; trust fracturing.

chapters.title: The Name Thief's Bargain
chapters.summary: Paloma tracks the defector and bargains for the stolen page, offering their own true name—the one thing keeping Vess's claim on them intact. The thief warns that Vess is not imprisoned; Vess is hiding from what it did. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice contemplated; faith cracking open.

chapters.title: Vess Speaks
chapters.summary: With the page recovered, Vess finally answers Paloma directly—warm, loving, monstrous—demanding the massacre be repeated to fuel the Hollow's opening. Paloma refuses for the first time in their life. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: the break; devotion curdling into clarity.

chapters.title: Excommunication
chapters.summary: Struck mute and half-blind by Vess's withdrawal, Paloma is nursed by Sera, who abandons her inquisitor's post to do it. They speak honestly for the first time since the conquest. POV: alternating Paloma and Sera. Emotional beat: tenderness without permission; love choosing itself over gods and crowns.

chapters.title: The Ledger Burns Slowly
chapters.summary: Ivetta declares Paloma oath-broken and bars them from the Hollow. Paloma begins settling debts independently, trading away their own memories—one per account—including the memory of Sera's face. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: grief as currency; paying for others with yourself.

chapters.title: Merrow's Bend Remembers
chapters.summary: The survivor's restored memory spreads like fire through the free cities: witnesses recall erased villages, massacres, the usurper's founding crime. Riots bloom. Justice arrives outside any court. POV: chorus of citizens, then Sera watching. Emotional beat: catharsis and terror; truth as contagion.

chapters.title: Sera's Choice
chapters.summary: The usurper orders Sera to burn the free cities' archives and take the Hollow by force. Instead she delivers the invasion plans to Ivetta, severing herself from the law forever. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: duty inverted; treason as fidelity to something truer.

chapters.title: The Door in the Hollow
chapters.summary: The guild opens the Hollow: a threshold of standing stones in a valley that appears on no map, breathing with the erased country beyond. Refugees begin crossing—but Vess waits on the other side, gathering strength from every prayer. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: fragile triumph; salvation with teeth.

chapters.title: What the God Did
chapters.summary: Crossing partially into the erased country, Paloma learns the full truth: Vess engineered its own erasure to escape judgment for devouring its worshippers' memories—the original sin the usurper built his throne upon. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: the bottom falling out; every certainty refunded.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Paloma writes the final ledger entry: all debts transferred to themselves, including the debt of a god. Ivetta, moved and broken, reopens the guild's doors to them. The armies breach the outer city. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: terrible resolve; accounting as absolution.

chapters.title: Judgment Outside the Law
chapters.summary: At the threshold, Paloma confronts Vess before the gathered refugees and the arriving armies: no trial, no throne, just the ledger read aloud. The crowd remembers what Vess devoured, and the god starves as its stolen memories return to their owners. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: climax; quiet, human justice overpowering the divine.

chapters.title: Holding the Door
chapters.summary: The Hollow begins collapsing as the usurper's forces flood the valley. Paloma takes Vess's place as the door's anchor, burning the last of their memories to keep it open while the free cities empty through. Sera refuses to leave. POV: Paloma and Sera. Emotional beat: sacrifice met with defiance; love refusing to be a debt.

chapters.title: A Country With No Name
chapters.summary: On the far side, in the erased country reborn unnamed, Paloma wakes with no past and Sera beside them, introducing herself as a stranger. The ledgers are blank; the first entry is theirs to write together. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: resolution; memory lost, love kept, freedom beginning on an empty page.
